name: Barnard's Star
tagline: The fastest star in the sky
blurb: The fastest-moving star in the sky: 10.4″ per year. Between SPHEREx visits it steps about 1–2 pixels; against the 2010 WISE image it has leapt almost 3 arcminutes.
notes: Too bright for SPHEREx: its centre saturates in nearly every exposure, so its spectrum is unreliable. Positions still work.

cube.note: SPHEREx all-sky spectral map: each channel is the average of every visit up to the release, so different channels at one spot come from different dates.

finecube.note: Built from the single SPHEREx exposures at 6.15" pixels: each channel averages every exposure whose wavelength at that spot falls in it, over all visits, so different channels come from different dates.

flags.meaning: percent of the visit's exposures on that detector flagged at the pixel (255 = not covered)

colour_hint: Barnard's Star is so bright that its centre is blown out (white) at most wavelengths, so its own colour can't be measured here. Its neighbours show the usual pattern: ordinary stars look blue in this view, because they are brightest at the shortest infrared wavelengths.

provenance.label: IRSA DR1+QR3 (baked 2026-11-15)
